# Fleet Principles {.unnumbered}

Part VI examines agentic systems at distributed fleet scale. When complex objectives require multiple autonomous entities to collaborate, the Stochastic Computer scales across clusters. We analyze multi-agent coordination under the Actor model and evaluate coordination overhead, instrument distributed execution graphs with OpenTelemetry semantic conventions for causal post-mortem debugging, and establish the macro-economics of accelerator fleet sizing via the Tokenomic Roofline model.

::: {#pri-vol3-stochastic-actors .callout-principle title="Distributed stochastic coordination"}

**Invariant**: Multi-agent collaboration is distributed computing over stochastic nodes subject to non-deterministic failure; unconstrained communication incurs an $O(M^2)$ coordination tax.

**Implication**: Systems must employ the Actor model with isolated state and hierarchical supervisor trees rather than unconstrained peer-to-peer conversational swarms.

:::

::: {#pri-vol3-trace-reconstructibility .callout-principle title="Deterministic trace reconstructibility"}

**Invariant**: Robust production operations require capturing non-deterministic environmental interactions into immutable event streams to enable bit-exact post-mortem replay and causal fault isolation.

**Implication**: Runtimes must implement OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions across all trajectory spans, logging token deltas, tool inputs/outputs, and latency profiles.

:::

::: {#pri-vol3-trajectory-goodput .callout-principle title="Trajectory goodput and fleet economics"}

**Invariant**: The governing metric of autonomous agent systems is Trajectory Goodput (verified task completions per dollar per GPU-hour), uniting compute efficiency and outcome accuracy.

**Implication**: Hardware fleet sizing and model routing must operate along the Pareto frontier, sizing accelerator pools for asymmetric prefill and decode phases.

:::
